\chapter{Build One Fictional Age Field}
\label{ch:pa-form-age-runway}
\hlchaptermodality{29}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can recognise the Gurmukhi age label and independently select and write one of two taught fictional age values from a nonverbal cue.}

The learner fills one fictional age line from a remembered cue with no romanization or copyable answer, then checks selection, digit order, spacing, and placement separately.
\end{chapteropening}

\section[u]{\pa{ਉ} — one new shape for the age label}

\label{lesson:PA-W07-independent-u}



\begin{quote}
Write the familiar \textbf{\pa{ਮ}} and \textbf{\pa{ਰ}} once each. The age label needs only one new letter before those known pieces can return.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Script — one tiny step}
Trace \textbf{\pa{ਉ}} slowly twice. It is the independent vowel \emph{u}. Do not assemble a word yet.

\subsection*{Your turn}
Cover the model, write \textbf{\pa{ਉ}} once, and repair only the first shape difference.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Stop after one new letter.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[umar]{\pa{ਉਮਰ} — assemble the age label}

\label{lesson:PA-W07-age-label}



\begin{quote}
Touch the pieces in order: \textbf{\pa{ਉ}}, \textbf{\pa{ਮ}}, \textbf{\pa{ਰ}}.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Script — one label}
Join \textbf{\pa{ਉ} + \pa{ਮ} + \pa{ਰ} = \pa{ਉਮਰ}}. On this fictional beginner form, \textbf{\pa{ਉਮਰ}} labels the age line. Copy the label once and leave the value blank.

\subsection*{Your turn}
Point to \textbf{\pa{ਉਮਰ}} and say what information belongs there. Do not add a number.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
No real personal information is requested.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[one]{\pa{੧} — the first Gurmukhi digit}

\label{lesson:PA-W07-digit-one}



\begin{quote}
Say the already-known Punjabi word for one: \textbf{\pa{ਇੱਕ}} (\emph{ikk}).
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Script — one digit}
Trace \textbf{\pa{੧}} twice. This is the Gurmukhi digit for 1. The spoken word was known; only the digit shape is new.

\subsection*{Your turn}
Cover the model and write \textbf{\pa{੧}} once.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
One digit is enough.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[two]{\pa{੨} — add the digit two}

\label{lesson:PA-W07-digit-two}



\begin{quote}
Write \textbf{\pa{੧}} and say the already-known Punjabi word for two: \textbf{\pa{ਦੋ}} (\emph{do}).
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Script — one digit}
Trace \textbf{\pa{੨}} twice. It is the Gurmukhi digit for 2.

\subsection*{Your turn}
Cover the model and write \textbf{\pa{੨}} once.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Stop after this second digit.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[five]{\pa{੫} — add the digit five}

\label{lesson:PA-W07-digit-five}



\begin{quote}
Write \textbf{\pa{੧}, \pa{੨}}. Say the already-known Punjabi word for five: \textbf{\pa{ਪੰਜ}} (\emph{panj}).
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Script — one digit}
Trace \textbf{\pa{੫}} twice. It is the Gurmukhi digit for 5.

\subsection*{Your turn}
Cover the model and write \textbf{\pa{੫}} once.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
The three needed digit shapes are now separate and known.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[15]{\pa{੧੫} — one fictional age value}

\label{lesson:PA-W07-age-fifteen}



\begin{quote}
Write \textbf{\pa{੧}}, then \textbf{\pa{੫}}, with a small gap.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Script — keep the digit order}
Close the gap: \textbf{\pa{੧} + \pa{੫} = \pa{੧੫}}, the digit entry 15. Left-to-right order matters. Copy this fictional age value once.

\subsection*{Your turn}
Cover the model, write 15 in Gurmukhi digits, then compare only digit order.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
This is invented practice data.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[25]{\pa{੨੫} — a second fictional age value}

\label{lesson:PA-W07-age-twenty-five}



\begin{quote}
Write \textbf{\pa{੨}}, then \textbf{\pa{੫}}, separately.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Script — reuse the same order rule}
Join them: \textbf{\pa{੨} + \pa{੫} = \pa{੨੫}}, the digit entry 25. Copy this fictional value once.

\subsection*{Your turn}
Cover the model, write 25 in Gurmukhi digits, and check digit order.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
The closed two-value bank is now fully taught.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[two fictional age cues]{Select one known age value}

\label{lesson:PA-W07-age-select}



\begin{quote}
Read the fictional bank once:

\begin{quote}
A — \textbf{\pa{੧੫}}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
B — \textbf{\pa{੨੫}}
\end{quote}
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Script — attach one cue to each value}
Point A to \textbf{\pa{੧੫}} and B to \textbf{\pa{੨੫}}. Cover the bank and select the value requested by B. Selection is separate from digit writing.

\subsection*{Your turn}
Reveal, point, cover, and select A once more. Do not fill the form yet.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
These cues belong only to this invented bank.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[age field]{Fill one supported age field}

\label{lesson:PA-W07-age-supported}



\begin{quote}
Keep the fictional bank visible: A — \textbf{\pa{੧੫}}, B — \textbf{\pa{੨੫}}.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Writing — model visible}
Complete \textbf{\pa{ਉਮਰ}: \_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_} for A. Read the label, select A, and copy \textbf{\pa{੧੫}}. This is supported entry, not independent writing evidence.

\subsection*{Your turn}
Compare selection, digit order, spacing, and placement in separate passes.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Stop after one supported line.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[age label and value boundary]{One clear boundary}

\label{lesson:PA-W07-age-spacing}



\begin{quote}
Read \textbf{\pa{ਉਮਰ}:\pa{੧੫}}. The label and value are both correct, but crowded.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Writing — repair only spacing}
Rewrite it as \textbf{\pa{ਉਮਰ}: \pa{੧੫}}. Keep one visible space after the colon. Change no digit and no letter.

\subsection*{Your turn}
Point once to the label, the boundary, and the value.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
One spacing repair is enough.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[age field after a short delay]{Hide, wait, then fill the age field}

\label{lesson:PA-W07-age-delayed}



\begin{quote}
Read A — \textbf{\pa{੧੫}}, B — \textbf{\pa{੨੫}} once. Hide the bank and count slowly to ten.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Writing — short delayed entry}
With the bank hidden, complete \textbf{\pa{ਉਮਰ}: \_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_} for B. Finish before revealing the bank.

\subsection*{Your turn}
Reveal and compare selection, digit order, spacing, then placement. Do not repair yet.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
One delayed line is enough.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[15 / 25]{Hear a number, write its Gurmukhi digits}

\label{lesson:PA-W07-age-dictation}



\begin{quote}
Hide every written value. This task checks digit transcription, not new Punjabi number words.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Writing — one support-language dictation cue}
Have a partner or screen reader say the support-language number \textbf{fifteen} once. Write only its Gurmukhi digits. No model is visible during the attempt.

\subsection*{Your turn}
Reveal \textbf{\pa{੧੫}} and compare the first digit, then the second digit. Repair only after the comparison.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Punjabi spoken forms beyond one to five remain future instruction.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[age-field repair]{Repair one dimension, then stop}

\label{lesson:PA-W07-age-repair}



\begin{quote}
For B, inspect \textbf{\pa{ਉਮਰ}: \pa{੫੨}}. The label and spacing are correct; digit order is not.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Writing — repair one named dimension}
Repair only digit order: \textbf{\pa{ਉਮਰ}: \pa{੨੫}}. Do not rewrite a correct label or boundary.

\subsection*{Your turn}
Name the four checks in order: selection, digit order, spacing, placement. Stop at the first mismatch.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
One bounded repair is enough.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[age field]{One no-model age field}

\label{lesson:PA-W07-age-no-model}



\begin{quote}
Close the previous lessons. There is no value bank, support-language label, or copyable digit answer below.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Writing — independent controlled choice}
Complete the requested fictional field:

\begin{quote}
A — \textbf{\pa{ਉਮਰ}: \_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_}
\end{quote}

Choose the known value attached to A and write it from memory. Do not reopen an earlier lesson until the attempt is complete.

\subsection*{Your turn — separate repair passes}
After writing, compare selection, digit order, spacing, and placement. Repair only the first differing dimension.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
This closes only the untimed age-field ladder. Phone, date, integration, and A1 readiness remain separate dependency-linked work.
\end{tcolorbox}
